plain_text:
2026 BOH draft minutes November 16, 2026 
  
Board members participating: Chair Celia Bird, Jenny Tomczak, Kate Tracy, Bianka 
Cimrin and staffed by Health Officer Bill Ward.    
  
Board Chair Celia Bird called the meeting to order at 5:53 pm.   
  
Agenda   
Bianka made a motion to amend the agenda to remove the “possible vote in item 4’s. and 
approve that as the agenda. Second by Bianka.  Unanimous vote in favor.      
 
Draft minutes  
Celia asked that her comments   Jenny noted that in the Health Equity item there was a typo in 
the transcription regarding “Oakdale Credential Center which was intended to say Overdose 
Prevention Center.  Jenny and Bianka noted typos to correct.  Jenny motioned to approve the 
draft minutes with the typos corrected.  Second by Bianka. Unanimous in favor. 
 
Public Forum     
No members of the public present. 
  
 
Substance Abuse and Safe Syringe Disposal  
Bianka updated the current document summarizing syringe report research and 
recommendations, which Celia will review before sharing with City Councilors or the board. Bill 
reached out to Councilor Litwin about the CDNR's progress with the syringe litter report and 
learned they completed their work, with an invitation to attend their December 16th meeting 
at 6 PM in the Bushor Conference room.  
Bianka agreed to speak about the syringe report at the CDNR meeting, and Celia will share the 
CDNR report with the team before the meeting. The discussion concluded with a question 
about potentially duplicating data between Secret Fix reports and medical center reports on 
needle sticks. 
 
 
Problem Property update 
Bill discussed recent developments with vacant properties in the city, including a bank on North 
Avenue that was purchased by Vermont Federal Bank and a property on Grove Street 
undergoing $800,000 in renovations. He explained the city's enforcement approach for non-
compliant properties, which includes a two-tiered fee system where fees increase for 
properties that remain vacant longer, with most properties paying between $200 and $1,500 
quarterly. Bill noted that while enforcement has been challenging, the city is seeing some 
positive results with properties coming into compliance, and he plans to present these updates 
at an upcoming press conference on Thursday.
Health Equity 
The group discussed supporting Burlington School District's playground design procedure with a 
focus on universal design and accessibility. Celia proposed that the board could take a broader 
role by researching how other cities implement universal design requirements and advocating 
for similar policies in Burlington. Bianka suggested the board could provide health and safety 
recommendations for playgrounds, including aspects like pest management, water access, and 
proper facilities. Bill will contact the Burlington Parks Department to see if a representative can 
participate in a future meeting to discuss universally accessible playground designs already in 
use by BPRW Department. 
 
Chair Report 
Celia updated the board that she had spoken with the BTV Clean-up crew leaders from the 
Peace and Justice Center.  She said they need to coordinate with Bill before installing some 
syringe disposal boxes that the Board supplied funding for.  Bill will reach out to them and 
report back.  
Emerging Issues  
Kate discussed potential engagement with UVM and the board discussed potential options.  
The board talked cold weather shelter policies and asked about having someone from CEDO 
present on the topic at an upcoming meeting.  Bill and Celia will work on an invitation to 
Rebecca Reese for the December meeting.   
 Public Outreach/Communications  
Bill will coordinate with Jane on outreach regarding how to report needle stick injuries, after 
confirming information with the Vermont Department of Health. 
 
 Adjournment    
The group scheduled their next meeting for December 7th at 5 PM at 645 Pine Street.  
Kate made a motion to adjourn the meeting, 2nd by Bianka.  
Celia adjourned the meeting at 6:55 p.m.
